class_definition.differs_beyond_the_top_level_clock_field: both parse as JSON objects and differ beyond the frozen clock names
class_definition.family_has_no_resolvable_twin: the family names no latest twin, or the named twin is not on disk
class_definition.identical_after_top_level_clock_strip: member and twin parse as JSON objects and are equal after removing the frozen clock names from the top level of both
class_definition.not_a_json_object: the member is not a .json payload (csv/md/jsonl): unmeasured, not a negative
class_definition.unreadable_member: the member is missing on disk or does not parse as JSON

method_limits: only four field names are forgiven (frozen_clock_fields); a family whose clock is spelled differently (run_at, written, asof-time) reads as differing even when it does not
the comparison is object equality after stripping: a list that gained or lost one element is a difference, so the identical count is a lower bound on semantic redundancy
non-json members are 100 of the 571 files and are published as unmeasured, never as a negative result
the population is E472's rows as published; a family that gained members since then is not rescanned here
identical payloads say nothing about whether the twin itself is read -- that is E479's question, and this face must not be read as a deletion licence

robustness.note: the frozen four names decide the verdict; this block only says whether a vintage ever differs from its twin on a date-shaped name alone
